checks.description: AWS root account access keys must not exist — root credentials bypass all IAM policies and give unrestricted account access
checks.impact: Root account access keys cannot be scoped by IAM policies. A compromised root key gives an attacker complete, irrevocable control of the AWS account including the ability to delete all users, disable CloudTrail, and destroy all resources.
checks.resolution: Delete the aws_iam_access_key resource referencing the root user. Use a least-privilege IAM user or role with only the permissions required for the task.
checks.errorMessage: aws_iam_access_key references the root user. Root account access keys must never be created — remove this resource and replace it with a least-privilege IAM user (CIS AWS v2.0 § 1.4)
